title: Lesson 3: Loving Your Church Family
description: God did not save you to follow Jesus alone. He placed you in a spiritual family where you are developed, cared for, corrected, encouraged, equipped for ministry, and sent on mission with others.

blocks.text: Lessons 1 and 2 moved outward through two connected homes: your neighbors next door and your family under your roof. Now we come to another home God gives His people: the local church. This lesson is about why belonging to a spiritual family is not optional for a growing disciple of Jesus.

blocks.title: Jonathan in the Wilderness
blocks.text:
David had been anointed as Israel's future king, but that did not make his life easy. Saul hunted him. Obedience became costly. The wilderness was lonely, dangerous, and confusing.

Jonathan could have treated David as a rival, but he became a brother. He warned David when danger was coming. He protected him when Saul wanted to kill him. He reminded David of God's promise when fear could have taken over. Jonathan did not just wish David well from a distance. He stood with him when faithfulness was hard.

Before the New Testament church had a name, Jonathan was already showing us something the church is meant to be. God often keeps His people faithful through faith-filled family. We need people who warn us, speak truth, stand with us, and point us back to God.
3.1 - Who has God used to warn, encourage, or strengthen you in your faith? Where are you tempted to try to follow Jesus alone?
The Church Is a Family, Not a Service

The church is not mainly a building, a Sunday event, a religious business, or a machine run by paid staff. The church is the adopted family of God. It is a people called together by Jesus, gathered around the gospel, and sent into the world with His love.

So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God... In him you also are being built together into a dwelling place for God by the Spirit.

In Christ, you are no longer a stranger looking in from the outside. You are a member of God's household. The local church is where that spiritual reality becomes visible and concrete. You are known, cared for, challenged, and given a real place in the family.
3.2 - What changes when you think about the local church as a spiritual family rather than a service you attend?
One Body, Many Members
For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ. For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body.

Paul's picture is physical on purpose. A body is not a crowd of disconnected parts sitting in the same room. The eye needs the hand. The head needs the feet. The weak parts receive honor and care. When one member suffers, all suffer together. When one member is honored, all rejoice together.

That means the church is not a restaurant where professionals serve and everyone else consumes. It is more like a family potluck. Everyone brings what they have, everyone receives from others, and the whole table is stronger because the Spirit is working through ordinary people.

3.3 - In Paul's body picture, what body part do you feel like right now and why? Do you feel visible like an eye, useful like a hand, unnoticed like a foot, weak and needing care, or disconnected from the rest of the body?
What the Early Church Looked Like

And they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers... And all who believed were together and had all things in common... And day by day, attending the temple together and breaking bread in their homes, they received their food with glad and generous hearts, praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved.

Acts 2 shows a church that loved God and their neighbors together. They gathered around teaching and prayer. They shared meals and needs. They remembered who God is and what He had done. They opened their lives to one another, and the Lord used their shared life as a witness to the world.

That is what a healthy church is meant to do. We learn to be God's satisfied children together. We bless others where we live, work, and play together. We belong as a welcoming spiritual family together. The big story of God is experienced together.
3.4 - When you read Acts 2, what part of church life do you most want more of right now: teaching, prayer, meals, generosity, shared needs, joy, worship, or mission together?
Why Connecting to a Local Church Matters

The Baptist Faith and Message describes a New Testament church as a local congregation of baptized believers joined by gospel covenant, governed by Christ's Word, practicing baptism and the Lord's Supper, using God-given gifts, and working to extend the gospel to the ends of the earth. In other words, church is not vague. It is local, committed, biblical, gifted, and missional.

That is why church membership matters. It gives assurance that your faith is not private and self-made. It gives you a base from which to care for others. It gives others a clear way to care for you. It helps leaders know whom they are responsible to shepherd. It strengthens our witness to unbelievers. And it helps us persevere when sin, suffering, or weariness make us want to drift.
And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together... but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.

A good church covenant is a promise to live as family on purpose. We regularly meet together, serve, encourage, warn, forgive, comfort, and suffer with one another. We include others through hospitality and generosity so they can see that they are welcome in God's family.
3.5 - Which part of a committed church family do you most need right now: care, correction, encouragement, accountability, a place to serve, mission with others, or help persevering?
When Church Has Hurt

Some people hear the word church and think of pain. Churches are made of sinners, and sometimes leaders or members wound people deeply. Connecting rightly to a local church does not mean pretending harm did not happen. It means bringing wounds into the light with wise, trustworthy believers, seeking protection where protection is needed, and letting Jesus heal you without giving up on His design for spiritual family.
Belonging That Blesses the World

A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another. By this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.

The church is a display of God's love. When believers forgive, carry burdens, cross normal social lines, and stay faithful through hard seasons, the world sees something of Jesus. We do not belong to a church only for our own care. We belong so we can love God and our neighbors together.
3.6 - What is one concrete step you could take in the next 30 days to connect more rightly to a local church or spiritual family?
This Week's Practice

Choose one step toward belonging this week. Attend a Sunday gathering and introduce yourself to someone. Ask about a neighborhood group, discipleship group, ministry team, or membership class. Text someone from church and ask how you can pray for them. If church has been painful for you, talk with a mature Christian or trusted leader about what a wise next step could be.
Lesson 3 Review

The church is not a machine, a restaurant, or a weekly event. It is the adopted family of God, the body of Christ, and a local people joined together by the gospel. In this family you are developed, cared for, corrected, encouraged, equipped, and sent. In the next lesson, you will look more closely at the gifts Jesus gives His people so each member can build up the body.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
